column5: You are standing on the equator, in a city by the sea.
It is a calm, warm morning.
But the ground beneath your feet is moving east at one thousand and thirty-seven miles per hour.
You never feel it, because everything moves together.
Now imagine the Earth begins to stop.
At first, it is only a breeze.
Loose paper drifts across the street.
Within minutes, the wind passes one hundred miles per hour.
At three hundred miles per hour, it is stronger than the worst tornado ever measured.
Whole floors tear away from the buildings.
Faster than the speed of sound.
The air and the oceans keep racing east.
The Earth itself would survive this.
Almost nothing standing on it would.
